title: security analysis
description: Scan this repository for API leaks and insecure coding exploits. Make sure I'm not going to get hacked setting this up.
close_reason: Completed pragmatic security review and applied hardening: timing-safe API key validation, admin rate limiting, placeholder API key rejection, dependency audit fix, and security setup guidance. Build, tests, and npm audit pass.

title: Normalize string input for Codex Responses
description: Codex upstream rejects public OpenAI Responses string input with 'Input must be a list'. Add normalization so /v1/responses accepts string input and converts it to a user input_text item before forwarding to Codex, preserving existing array input behavior.
close_reason: Normalized Codex Responses string input to a user input_text array while preserving array input behavior; verified focused tests, build, and full suite.

title: Add durable Responses e2e smoke artifacts
description: Capture the successful auth2api /v1/responses runtime checks as reusable end-to-end smoke artifacts: one non-streaming request and one streaming request using the configured API key and gpt-5.5.
close_reason: Added reusable non-streaming and streaming /v1/responses e2e script, npm entry, and README usage; verified with live gpt-5.5 runtime.

title: Document and script Docker Codex deployment
description: Add a clear local/remote Docker sequence for real Codex use: build/load image, mount config.yaml correctly, run Codex login into the same Docker data volume, start the service, and verify health/accounts/models. Include small scripts where useful so users do not have to assemble docker run commands manually.
close_reason: Added Docker Codex deployment scripts for login, run, and verification; documented correct config/volume sequence and manual equivalent. Verified shell syntax, npm run build, npm test, and HOST_PORT=18317 npm run test:docker.

title: Add local Docker build smoke test workflow
description: Add a local workflow for building the Docker image and smoke testing it. Include any required test configuration, such as a safe temporary config.yaml/auth-dir setup, container run command, health check, and minimal authenticated endpoint check so users can verify the image works without exposing real OAuth tokens.
close_reason: Added local Docker smoke-test workflow with temporary config/token setup, localhost-bound container run, health/auth/model checks, README usage, and npm shortcut. Verified npm run build and HOST_PORT=18317 npm run test:docker.

title: Optimize Dockerfile runtime image
description: Reduce Docker runtime image size and attack surface: use reproducible npm install with package-lock.json, avoid shipping dev dependencies, add a .dockerignore, and run the app as a non-root user where feasible.
close_reason: Optimized Docker build to use npm ci from package-lock.json, copy only production dependencies into the runtime image, exclude unnecessary build context with .dockerignore, and run as the node user with writable /data and /config directories. Verified with npm run build and docker image checks.

title: Populate output in streaming Codex response.completed
description: Codex streaming Responses emits output_item.done events but response.completed.response.output is empty. Investigate whether the proxy should enrich the final streaming response.completed event with collected output items for stricter OpenAI Responses compatibility, without breaking pass-through SSE behavior.
notes: Current evaluation 2026-05-28: still relevant, but narrowly scoped. Non-stream /v1/responses already reconstructs completed.output from response.output_item.done events and has smoke coverage. Streaming /v1/responses still uses handleStreamingResponse passthrough, so Codex response.completed events can still contain response.output: [] even though output_item.done events were sent earlier. Keep open if strict streaming Responses clients need final response.completed.response.output populated; otherwise it can be deferred/closed as pass-through-compatible behavior.
